transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess what made me come in is that I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm a total fake in my apprenticeship. I'm a pipefitter apprentice, and I just feel like I'm constantly letting my family and the younger apprentices down over stuff that... I don't know, I know other people would probably just fix it and move on from it. 

Like the other day, we were working on this commercial boiler system. Have you ever seen the inside of one of those? It's actually crazy how much pressure they hold, the valves are massive. My dad used to work on them back in the nineties before everything went digital, and he actually gave me his old pipe wrenches when I got my associate's degree. They're super heavy cast iron. You can't even buy them like that anymore, everything is aluminum now so it's lighter on your toolbelt. My belt gets so heavy it actually bruises my hips if I wear it too long, especially when I have my heavy tape measure clipped to the side. 

But... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. I just feel guilty all the time, like I'm a fraud on the job and letting everyone down.
Do you find that you often get sidetracked like that in conversations or tasks, and have trouble refocusing back on what you were doing?

Um, I guess sometimes? Like, I don't really notice it happening until I'm already talking about something else. It's just that everything reminds me of something else, you know? Like how you asked about getting sidetracked, and it makes me think about this one time we were laying out the tracks for a radiant heating system in this huge custom home. The blueprints were an absolute mess. The architect had drawn the zones all wrong, and I was trying to explain to the general contractor why we couldn't just run the PEX tubing the way he wanted because the heat distribution would be totally uneven. 

PEX is great, though. It's so much easier to work with than rigid copper, plus you don't have to sweat the joints, which is a lifesaver when you're working in tight crawlspaces. I hate crawlspaces. I found a dead raccoon in one once, and the smell was... ugh, I can't even describe it. It took three days to get the smell out of my coveralls, even after washing them twice with baking soda. My mom swore by baking soda for everything. She used to make this paste with it for bee stings when I was a kid. 

But, um... wait. Refocusing. Right. Yeah, I guess I do have trouble with that sometimes. I'm not really sure if it's a big problem, though. I just have a lot on my mind.
Thinking back, did you have this same kind of trouble staying focused and getting sidetracked when you were a kid in school, or is this something that's only been happening recently?

Um, when I was a kid? I don't really know. I don't think so? I mean, school was okay, I guess. I actually really liked shop class in high school. Mr. Henderson was the teacher, and he was the one who actually told me I should look into the trades instead of just going to a four-year college like everyone else. He was missing half of his left index finger from a table saw accident, which you'd think would make him super strict about safety, but he was actually pretty chill. 

He let me build this really cool cedar chest for my final project. Cedar smells so good. We have this huge cedar tree in our front yard at home, and every fall it drops all these little brown sprigs everywhere. Raking them is the worst because they get stuck in the tines of the rake. My dad bought this fancy ergonomic rake last year, but I still think the old metal ones work better, even if they're heavier. It's kind of like the pipe wrenches, you know? The old stuff is just built to last. 

But, uh, school. Yeah. I don't really remember getting sidetracked a lot back then. I think this is more of a recent thing.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling consistently sad, down, or empty most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, sad? I guess I do feel down a lot lately. Just sort of empty, like you said. Especially when I'm driving home from the job site. The commute is brutal right now because they're doing all this construction on I-95. They've had the left lane closed for like three months, and the traffic just backs up for miles. 

I usually try to listen to podcasts to pass the time. I found this really good one about the history of deep-sea diving. Did you know the first diving suits were made of leather and weighed like 200 pounds? The helmets alone were solid copper. It's crazy to think about someone going underwater in that. It kind of reminds me of working in those deep utility trenches, where you're surrounded by all this heavy dirt and shoring boxes. Shoring is so important, though. A guy on a different crew got partially buried last year because they didn't slope the trench right, and it took them hours to dig him out. He's okay now, but he transferred to doing strictly residential work after that. Residential is definitely less stressful, but the pay isn't as good, and you have to deal with homeowners hovering over you while you work. 

But, um, feeling sad. Yeah. I guess I have been feeling pretty down most days lately. It just feels like I can't shake it.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your hobbies or spending time with family, over these past couple of weeks?

Um, yeah, I guess so. Like, lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook and not even care. I used to draw all the time, especially, like, pipe layouts and isometric drawings just for fun, or, well, actual art too. But now I just... don't. And I've been skipping my rec volleyball league, too. The gym where we play has this terrible HVAC system. The ductwork is completely exposed, which looks cool, I guess, kind of industrial, but the air return is positioned right over the bleachers, so it's always freezing if you sit there. 

I was actually looking at the spiral ducting last time I was there, and you could tell the seams were starting to separate. They probably used cheap mastic sealant instead of doing it right. Mastic is okay for small jobs, but if you're running commercial air, you really need to tape and seal it properly or you lose so much efficiency. It's like when people try to DIY their plumbing and use compression fittings behind a wall. You never put a compression fitting where you can't see it, because it's going to leak eventually. Water always finds a way out. I spent three hours last month fixing a ceiling because some guy tried to run his own ice maker line and flooded his entire kitchen. The drywall was completely mush. Drywall dust is the worst, it gets in your hair and you feel gritty for days. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, my hobbies. Yeah, I've been ignoring the group texts for my volunteer stuff, too. I just don't feel much of anything about it anymore, even though all that stuff used to make me feel like, you know, myself.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off dead during this time?

Um, no, I don't have some plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... I don't know, sometimes when I'm driving home after class, or just lying awake at night, I get these thoughts that it would be easier if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. 

Lying awake is the worst, honestly. My apartment is right next to this intersection where the traffic light is on a timer instead of a sensor, so cars just sit there idling at 3 AM for absolutely no reason. You can hear the bass from their stereos vibrating through the walls. It drives me crazy because I tried to soundproof my bedroom window with this weatherstripping foam, but the gap was too wide. I probably need to just replace the whole sash, but my landlord is so cheap. He wouldn't even pay for a real plumber when the toilet in the unit upstairs started leaking into my bathroom. He sent his brother-in-law, who tried to fix a cracked PVC flange with silicone caulk. Silicone! I told him it wasn't going to hold, and sure enough, three days later I had water dripping onto my bath mat. 

I ended up fixing it myself because I couldn't stand looking at it. I had to cut out the old flange and solvent-weld a new one in. The primer they use for PVC has this really strong, sweet chemical smell. It always gives me a headache if I don't ventilate the room enough. You're supposed to use a fan, but my bathroom doesn't even have an exhaust vent, which I'm pretty sure is a code violation. 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, no plans to hurt myself. Just... sometimes wishing I wouldn't wake up.
